**Tidepool — Build Plan**

**Design system (carried from reference):** deep forest green (#1B3A2F) base, coral (#FF6F5E) accents, warm off-white paper texture. Fraunces (serif) for headlines, Inter for body, IBM Plex Mono reserved for pull quotes and annotations. A conceptual spine: the page itself is structured as a week.

**1. Hero + week sidebar.** Left rail: vertical timeline with seven day-nodes (Mon–Sun); a coral ring marks "Mon — Plan." Main column: one long serif headline in the reference's run-on style: *"Give your small team one shared view of the week that fills itself in as plans shift, flags conflicts before anyone books over anyone, and makes Friday's recap write itself so nobody opens Monday asking what we're doing."* Hand-drawn coral arrow curls from headline to a tilted app screenshot with soft shadow.

**2. Trust strip.** Six grayscale customer logotypes on off-white, one row, no copy.

**3. "The week, mapped."** Tue–Thu sidebar nodes anchor three alternating image/text splits: shared calendar blocks, async status updates, conflict alerts. Each gets a coral line-art illustration, no stock photos.

**4. Pull quote.** Full-bleed forest-green band, off-white monospace: *"We cancelled the Monday meeting. The week just… appears."* Coral attribution, small round avatar.

**5. Metrics trio.** Cream background, three oversized serif numerals: "4 hrs saved weekly," "92% of plans kept," "2,100 teams."

**6. Closing CTA.** Timeline resolves at a filled coral node, "Fri — Done." Headline: "Plan next week in one sitting." Solid coral button "Start free," ghost button "Watch the 2-minute demo."

**7. Footer.** Slim forest-green bar, monospace link set.

**Copy approach:** second-person plural, calm and concrete; verbs about rhythm, visibility, and time returned; zero exclamation marks; feature names drawn from Tidepool vocabulary (tides, currents) used sparingly.
final:
**Tidepool — Revised Build Plan**

**System:** Forest green #1B3A2F, coral #FF6F5E, plus warm sand #F3ECE1 as neutral (60/30/10). Fraunces / Inter / IBM Plex Mono. The structural conceit now runs the whole page: the day-rail never leaves the left edge, every section *is* a day, and nodes fill coral as you scroll past. Hand-drawn coral annotations (arrows, underlines, margin scrawl) recur throughout like a teammate marking up the plan. Mobile: rail collapses to a dot strip beneath the header.

**1. Hero — Mon, "Plan."** Run-on serif headline: *"Give your small team one shared view of the week that fills itself in as plans shift, flags collisions before anyone double-books, and writes Friday's recap for you — so Monday never starts with 'wait, what are we doing?'"* Coral arrow annotated *"the whole product →"* points to a tilted screenshot. CTA pair moved above the fold.

**2. Proof strip — Mon.** Logos plus one humanizing line: *"2,100 teams stopped holding status meetings."*

**3. Live demo — Tue.** One full-width looping capture replaces three feature cards: drag a task, the week reflows, a conflict flag pops. Margin note: *"There is no refresh button."*

**4. Capabilities — Wed.** Three tight splits, named as behaviors: **Tides** (the weekly rhythm that rebuilds itself), **Currents** (async check-ins), **Drift Alerts** (double-bookings flagged Tuesday, not discovered Friday).

**5. Pull quote — Wed.** Full-bleed green band, off-white mono: *"We cancelled our Monday meeting three months ago. Nobody's noticed — except the calendar."*

**6. Metrics — Thu.** Sand background, oversized serif: *"4.2 hrs returned weekly," "92% of plans survive contact with Tuesday," "0 status meetings required."*

**7. Integrations — Thu.** Slim row (Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, Linear), each tagged with a one-word mono annotation: *"synced," "read-only."*

**8. Close — Fri, "Done."** Rail resolves to one solid coral node. *"Plan next week in one sitting."* Solid coral "Start free," ghost "Watch the 2-minute demo," scrawled: *"takes 11 minutes."*

**9. Footer.** Green bar, mono links, one easter egg: *"Next high tide: Mon 9:00."*

**Copy approach:** second-person plural; verbs of rhythm and visibility; no exclamation marks; tide vocabulary capped at the three feature names.

*What got stronger: the rail now structures the entire page; annotations became a system; one live demo beats three cards; CTAs arrive earlier.*
